title: Alias Registry + Telemetry-driven Compatibility Shim for Tool/Function Interop
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Introduce an Alias Registry service and a lightweight compatibility shim to unify OpenAI-style tool names and Redwood legacy function names at runtime. Goal is to provide: fast deterministic name resolution for latency-sensitive streaming/tool-calls, reversible alias mappings for auditability, telemetry-driven alias pruning and scoring, and a migration/backfill path so existing customer integrations continue to work without changes.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime resolves tool/function identifiers within 500µs p50 for the 95% traffic path with the registry cache enabled
Alias mappings are reversible and persisted with origin/created_by metadata for auditing
Telemetry surfaces top-20 ambiguous aliases and a confidence score; alias pruning job can be gated and rolled back
Compatibility shim is exercised by e2e tests covering streaming tool calls, non-streaming synchronous calls, and function-call fallbacks
No customer-reported integrations breakage during canary (automated smoke tests pass for top 10 known mappings)
implementation_plan:
1) Design: canonical name format and alias scoring algorithm (exact > normalized > fuzzy embedding similarity).
2) Service: implement alias-registry HTTP API with versioned namespaces and metadata (origin, created_at, confidence).
3) Runtime integration: add in-process LRU cache + async refresh; fast-path exact match and normalized match before fuzzy/telemetry path.
4) Migration: build backfill script to ingest legacy function registry and map to tool descriptors.
5) Telemetry: emit resolution events, ambiguity counters, and latency histograms.
6) Tests: unit, integration, and e2e against streaming and function-call harness.
7) Rollout: staged canary -> region rollout -> global with rollback flag.
migration_plan:
- Snapshot current legacy function registry and existing tool manifest.
- Run batch matcher that applies deterministic normalizations (case, punctuation, snake/kebab/camel conversions) and records candidate aliases with scores.
- Persist candidate aliases in alias-registry with source tag 'backfill-2026-02'.
- Run automated smoke test suite against canary customers and top-100 customer integrations.
- If smoke passes, promote alias set to 'active' and enable runtime fast-path resolution.
- Keep aliases TTL'd and subject to telemetry pruning (configurable 30/60/90 days).
rollout_plan:
Phase A (dev): internal runtime builds with registry disabled by default, run integration tests.
Phase B (canary): enable alias-registry for 5% internal traffic and 3 developer orgs; monitor ambiguity metrics and latency.
Phase C (customer canary): opt-in for selected customers with known legacy functions; run cross-checks and collect feedback.
Phase D (gradual): increment traffic 10% increments with feature flag, revert on increased error/latency thresholds.
Fallback: runtime config to prefer legacy lookup; immediate disable flips to exact legacy resolution path.

notes: Key trade-offs: fuzzy matching increases false positives; to mitigate we will require a confidence threshold and human review for aliases created by backfill with low confidence. For latency-sensitive streaming we only use exact and normalized matches; fuzzy fallback only applies to non-stream fast-paths or after a short async re-resolution. The registry is intentionally small (tens of thousands of aliases) and will be regionally sharded to keep lookup latency low.
